entries.title: The Unexpected Diagnosis
entries.body:
Like I mentioned in my introduction, I was planning to work as an engineer someday but God had a different plan for me. I was, all of a sudden, diagnosed with a brain tumor. To make matters worse, it was next to my brain stem, so it was inoperable. I was told that I would live only for a few more months.

But praise God because I already knew my Saviour and what He was capable of doing. I didn't have any "why" or "why now" questions back then. I already knew that only God could heal me. And even if He chooses not to do anything, He knows exactly what He is doing with His creation, His daughter, His apple of the eye.

entries.title: A Medical Marvel
entries.body:
Many doctors advised us against a surgery... they said I would slip into a coma, be paralysed, or there was an 80% chance that I would lose one of the senses at least. But as soon as we got to know about the tumor, we all started fasting and praying.

I came out of the surgery as a winner by God’s grace! I was a miracle! In just three months’ time, I was back doing all things, was back travelling long hours, studying, and doing my submissions. Everything was good. I became closer to God, sharing my testimony, and encouraging people.

entries.title: The Tumor Returns
entries.body: In December 2011, a routine MRI showed the tumor growing, and I had to undergo radiations immediately. Though the news was very depressing and I began questioning, I went ahead with it because I knew God was with me. In a couple of months, I started going back to college and I thought I was fine.

entries.title: A Season of Pain
entries.body:
I fell sick again and this time it was bad. I had all these "why" questions in my head... I just had four papers left to complete my graduation. My condition was worsening, and I remember thinking I wouldn’t make it to my 23rd birthday.

I was put on high dose medications, and though my symptoms were controlled, it had a negative effect on my body. I started swelling weirdly, my skin started tearing... I would hardly see the mirror because I would start crying looking at myself. Three months passed and there was no improvement. Another MRI revealed that the tumor was growing and I needed a surgery immediately.

entries.title: Trusting His Plan
entries.body:
The doctors said the risk involved with this surgery was twice the first one. Everyone everywhere, including my church, started fasting and praying for me. 21 days of continuous prayer was held at my place. My condition began worsening... I couldn’t eat or sleep properly, started losing sensation on the left side of my body, experienced partial facial paralysis, and lost my balance and speech.

We prayed and went ahead with the surgery on 17th July 2012. My chances of survival were very less... but praise God that I did survive it! Jeremiah 29:11 says, "For I know the plans I have for you... plans to give you hope and a future." It gives you the strength to endure everything.

entries.title: A God of Restoration
entries.body:
Today, by God's immense grace, I am much better. I knew all about God but now... I KNOW HIM!! And honestly, I praise God for the things that I went through because I didn't lose anything, I just gained His immense peace, His love, His grace, His mercy, and His compassion. Our God is a God of restoration!

I could write my remaining 4 papers of engineering and complete my graduation. Today, my goals have changed. I live to please God, to not lose my focus from Jesus, from eternity! I will try hard simply because I love Him and want Him to smile looking at His daughter.
